newsitem.title: USA: Gliatech says has Japan deal for ADCON.
newsitem.headline: Gliatech says has Japan deal for ADCON.

text.p: Gliatech Inc said Monday that Japan's Chugai Pharmaceutical Co Ltd has signed a development and exclusive license agreement to use and sell Gliatech's ADCON products in Japan.
Chugai will fund and conduct clinical trials and seek regulatory approval to market the anti-adhesion barrier gels in Japan, Gliatech said in a statement.
The gels were developed to inhibit surgical scarring and adhesion. One type is for back surgery, another is for tendon and peripheral nerve surgery and others are planned, it said.
Gliatech stock closed up 3/4 at 10 on Nasdaq.
Both products are being sold as medical devices in Europe and elsewhere, and clinical trials are under way in the United States, Gliatech said.
"We are extremely pleased to have Chugai as our development and marketing partner in Japan," said Thomas Oesterling, Gliatech president and chief executive officer.

Masao Sugiura, the general manager of Chugai's medical device division, said, "We are very excited about the opportunity." Chugai has developed drugs for cancer, bone metabolism and cardiovascular and cerebrovascular disorders and has sales of about $2 billion, Gliatech said.
